title: 약국에서 감기약 사기
summary: A customer with a cold describes their symptoms at a Korean pharmacy and buys cold medicine without a prescription.
objective: Learners can state symptoms ('-이/가 아파요', '-이/가 나요'), understand dosing instructions (하루 ~ 번, 한 번에 ~ 알씩, 식후에), and check them with '~ 먹으면 돼요?'
exercises: The pharmacist says: '하루 두 번, 한 번에 한 알씩 드세요.' How many tablets do you take in one day? Answer in English or Korean.
Your throat hurts and you have a cough. Answer the pharmacist's question '어디가 불편하세요?' in one sentence. Join the two symptoms with '-고'.
The pharmacist asks '언제부터 그러셨어요?' Your symptoms started the day before yesterday. Give a short answer ending in '-부터요'.
Write this instruction in Korean the way a pharmacist would say it: 'Take it twice a day, after meals.'
You think the pharmacist said to take two tablets at a time, but you're not sure. Ask a question to check. End it with '먹으면 돼요?', like the customer does in the dialogue.
answers: 한 번에 두 알씩 먹으면 돼요?

dialogue.meaning: Welcome. What seems to be the problem?
My throat hurts and I have a runny nose.
Since when has it been like that?
Are you taking any other medicine?

dialogue.korean: 그럼 이 감기약 드세요. 하루 세 번, 한 번에 한 알씩 식후에 드세요.
dialogue.meaning: Then take this cold medicine. Take one tablet at a time, three times a day, after meals.
So I take it after I eat?
Yes, that's right. Take it after you eat.

words.meaning: to feel unwell (in part of the body)
words.exampleMeaning: My stomach feels a bit upset.
I cough a lot at night.
Could I get some cold medicine?
You just take it three times a day.
Make sure you take this medicine after eating.
I went to the doctor the day before yesterday.
